Glossary

Backlink: what is it, exactly?

A backlink is a link placed on another website that leads to yours. For Google, it is a bit like a neighbour recommending you: the more serious the source and the closer to your trade, the more the recommendation counts.

The definition in one sentence

When the tourist office website writes “stay at the gîte des Tilleuls” and those words lead to your website, that is a backlink for you. The English word means a link pointing back.

The other way round, a link from your website to another one is an outbound link, and a link between two of your own pages is an internal link.

What it does for a small business

Backlinks play two roles:

  • They bring visitors, who click from a site they already use.
  • They boost your credibility in Google’s eyes, as it sees them as a sign that others trust you.

For a local business, a few good, well placed links are worth far more than a mountain of dubious ones.

Natural links for a small business

  • The website of your town hall or local council, in its business directory.
  • Your chamber of trades or chamber of commerce, your trade body.
  • Suppliers or partners who list their resellers.
  • The local newspaper, if it covers your opening or an event.
  • The associations you support, the sports club you sponsor.

A real-life example

A beekeeper sells his honey at markets. He asks the producers’ market website, the grocer who resells his honey and the beekeepers’ association to add a link to his page. Three links, all logical, all tied to his trade. That is exactly the kind of signal Google likes.

What to avoid

  • Buying links in bulk. These offers put your link on unrelated sites, and Google can penalise you.
  • Endless link swaps with just anyone.
  • Comments stuffed with links on blogs or forums.

A good backlink has to be earned. The simplest way is often to have something to show: some news, a skill, a real partnership.

Your questions

Do links from social media count?

They bring visitors, which is already good, but Google usually gives them little weight for ranking. They are still useful for making your website known.

Can a bad link harm me?

A single link from a dubious site usually has no effect, as Google knows how to ignore it. The risk comes when someone tries to cheat with links bought or churned out in bulk.
